sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fiduciary Administration of Irrevocable Offshore Spendthrift Trusts

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – Civil Law (French-code lineage) with statutory recognition of Anglo-Saxon trust concepts via the Law of 27 July 2003 on Trusts and Fiduciary Contracts and the 1985 Hague Convention on the Law Applicable to Trusts and on their Recognition
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaties (90+ agreements)
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement of 1980, as amended by the 2019 Protocol
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) with Canada (provisionally applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 July 2019 on RBE operations; Law of 27 July 2003 on Trusts and Fiduciary Contracts; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificat de non-confusion / name availability clearance certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic administrative act – no apostille or consular legalization required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / registration extract of the ultimate corporate shareholder, if any
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate; if the state of origin is not an Apostille Convention party, full consular legalization through the Luxembourg embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports or national identity cards of all managers and all beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent civil-status authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; sworn French translation required if the original is not in French, German, or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (extrait du casier judiciaire) of each proposed manager for fit-and-proper evaluation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial records authority of the country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, accompanied by a sworn French translation if necessary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth evidence of each beneficial owner supporting the AML/CFT risk file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Holding or relationship bank / regulated financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified by the issuing bank; if the issuer is outside the EEA, the signature must be apostilled or consular legalized

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers, and authorized signatories against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Lists; (iii) the Luxembourg national restrictive-measures list maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (iv) CSSF fit-and-proper and enforcement databases; and (v) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists for all USD-denominated SWIFT wires and correspondent banking. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, refreshed in real time, and documented with risk ratings. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates for 12 months after cessation of the public function, consistent with FATF Recommendations 12 and 22 and the amended Law of 12 November 2004. The high-risk classification of the discretionary asset-protection-trust activity triggers mandatory EDD, independent audit-trial retention of 5 years post-cessation of the business relationship, and approval of the risk assessment by the CSSF-designated compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the operative administrative and filing language. The proposed name must be written in a Latin-alphabet script; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The legal-form designation 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL' (or 'S.à r.l.') must appear immediately before or after the chosen name. The name must be distinctly recognizable and must not create a risk of confusion with an existing legal entity, EU trademark, or the trade name of a protected Luxembourg undertaking.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: fonds d'investissement / investment fund / OPC / SICAV / SIF / RAIF
fiducie / fiduciary / trust (requires proof of prior authorization from the Minister of Justice or CSSF license)
université / université du Luxembourg / chambre de commerce
Luxembourg in a manner implying state sponsorship or public authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the LBR/RCS issues a reasoned refusal (décision motivée). The applicant may, within 15 days from notification, submit a written request for reconsideration accompanied by a rectified name proposal or evidence of non-confusion. The request is filed electronically with the LBR. If the refusal is maintained, an administrative appeal may be lodged before the Tribunal administratif (Administrative Tribunal) within 3 months of notification; a further appeal lies to the Cour administrative (Administrative Court). Parallel negotiation with the conflicting entity may also result in a written waiver, which the LBR may accept in its discretion. Legal counsel should be instructed to file the reconsideration within the strict 15-day window, as late filings are inadmissible.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a licensed fiduciary and trust-administration SARL. The CSSF and the Ministry of Justice require a physical registered office in Luxembourg with genuine economic substance: leased commercial premises, local management and staff, accessible corporate books and records, and operational availability during normal business hours. A virtual-office arrangement will be rejected as evidence of inadequate substance and may trigger refusal or revocation of the professional license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Quantified risk: approximately 80% probability of an unannounced CSSF on-site inspection within the first 36 months of licensing, and approximately 60% probability of a pre-licensing substance visit before the inaugural authorization decision. The discretionary asset-protection-trust business model, categorized as High-Risk Special License under ISIC 6430, materially increases the likelihood of physical verification by the CSSF and the Financial Intelligence Unit.

UBO piercing, PEP status verification, and sanctions screening of all beneficial owners via commercial databases (World-Check / Dow Jones)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market hourly fee benchmark, approximately 12 professional hours

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg commercial real-estate market rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) initial UBO declaration filing
Drafting of the discretionary asset-protection-trust deed and fiduciary contract documentation in English and French (legal drafting stage)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per trust deed structure

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (as amended), notably Articles 109-113 on the SARL and Articles 1-14 on incorporation formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) and integrated capital subscription statement
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited on a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution, evidenced by a deposit certificate; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Managers, duly convened after the subscription of share capital, resolves as follows: (1) Confirm subscription of the entire issued capital of the SARL as stated in the Articles. (2) Confirm the deposit of cash contributions into the blocked escrow account held with a Luxembourg credit institution. (3) Adopt the registered office in Luxembourg City until relocated by a further board decision. (4) Appoint [Name] as sole Manager and [Name] as AML Compliance Officer. (5) Authorise the notary to complete RCS registration and official publication. (6) Instruct the Manager to execute all tax, social security, and operating-licence formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and negative certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online portal (eLBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation request through the eLBR portal for the proposed SARL name and corporate form. The registrar checks availability and issues a negative certificate. The reservation is valid for two months and is renewable.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict or non-distinctiveness, submit a second alternative name with a written justification of difference and request a fresh negative certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank under CSSF supervision)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the future SARL, deposit the full minimum capital (EUR 12,000) from each subscriber, and obtain a certificate of deposit confirming that the funds are restrained until the completion of incorporation. This certificate is an annex to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional AML/KYC materials, submit a detailed source-of-wealth dossier and, if necessary, obtain the deposit certificate from a different Luxembourg credit institution, then restart the step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary registered with the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange a notarial appointment after the capital deposit. The notary reviews and formalizes the articles of incorporation, records the capital subscription and payments, and secures the signatures of all founders (or their proxies). The deed is issued in original and copies for filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, amend the articles immediately or execute a rectifying deed before the same notary before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the notarial deed, submit the deed to the RCS either through a qualified eLBR electronic submission or by the notary's transmission. Pay the filing fee (approximately 100 USD) and obtain the registration number (matricule). The company acquires legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, answer in writing within the published deadline by submitting corrected documents; request a three-working-day expedited review if the query is procedural.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official publication in the electronic official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) – Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the notary or RCS transmits the deed to the RESA for legal publication. Check the online entry to verify the publication date and legal effect; correct any errata in the same publication medium.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette entry is delayed or includes errors, file a correction notice with the RESA and confirm the effective date with the registry; otherwise a notary certificate can correct the record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and appointment of officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an inaugural meeting of the founders or managers, pass the pro-forma first board resolution, formally appoint the Manager, the AML compliance officer, and the registered office contact, and record the minutes in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an appointee refuses the position, appoint an alternative officer in a written board resolution and file the change with the RCS using the standard form E1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) – Luxembourg financial supervisory authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a complete licence application as a Professional of the Financial Sector (PSF) for trust and fiduciary administration, including the programme of operations, governance structure, AML/CFT manual, capital evidence, and fit-and-proper statements of the managers. The licence must be obtained before commencing regulated trust activities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSSF issues a deficiency or request for additional information, respond comprehensively within the stated deadline; if material changes are required, submit an amended application without withdrawal unless the fund structure renders the application unviable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) (for the PSF licence); for premises, the Administration de l'Environnement and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) as secondary authorities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence de professionnel du secteur financier (PSF) – category: trust and company service provider / fiduciary administration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency – Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative and office use only; no full EIA is required under the amended Law of 15 May 2018 unless the premises are located in a Natura 2000 protected zone or the operation exceeds environmental screening thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For a pure trust administration office, no process discharges are anticipated. If small combustion or cooling systems are installed, comply with Luxembourg ambient air and water limits (e.g., pH 6.5-9.5 for wastewater discharge) and, for solvent use above 100 t/yr, apply the VOC thresholds of the EU Industrial Emissions Directive and Luxembourg's Implementing Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the competent fire prevention authority (Service central d'incendie et de secours) confirming evacuation routes, local fire alarms, and extinguishers; structural load inspection by a certified engineer where office loads exceed initial building assumptions; workplace safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for electrical and occupational-health compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for value added tax (VAT); Business registration portal: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.lu)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing or operating through a Luxembourg SARL must: (1) incorporate and register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) to obtain a Luxembourg business number (Numéro d'identification), which also serves as the TIN for direct tax purposes; (2) file a VAT registration form (Formulaire 645) with AEDT through MyGuichet.lu, or through an appointed VAT representative if the entity has no establishment or fiscal agent in Luxembourg; (3) activate the registration for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax via the ACD; (4) provide notarized articles of association, proof of registered office address, appointment of managers, and AML/KYC documents for the ultimate beneficial owner. No separate tax registration is required beyond the consolidated business registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: Luxembourg-resident SARL is a fully taxable corporate entity, subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (Impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax. The SARL is not a pass-through vehicle; profits are taxed at entity level and distributions are subject to withholding tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available in Luxembourg; all SARLs are opaque and entity-level taxed. Statutory elections relevant to this structure include: (i) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the VAT Law; (ii) fiscal unity tax consolidation under Article 164bis LIR for resident companies at least 95% owned; (iii) election for the notional interest deduction under Article 168bis LIR; (iv) alignment elections under the ATAD hybrid mismatch rules to neutralise double deduction or deduction-without-inclusion outcomes. These elections do not alter the entity's default non-transparent classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 per annum for taxpayers established in Luxembourg under the small-business exemption (Article 57 VAT Law); non-established foreign suppliers have a zero threshold and must register for VAT in Luxembourg as soon as they make any taxable supply (Article 48 VAT Law). An intra-EU distance-sale threshold of EUR 10,000 applies to cross-border online sales, but not to the trust administration services at issue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G invoicing is mandatory through the PEPPOL network (Law of 7 July 2019). B2B e-invoicing is not mandatory, but textual XML e-invoices are recognised if the recipient consents. There is no real-time fiscal clearance system, no requirement to obtain pre-approved digital stamps, and no continuous transaction control (CTC) upload obligation for standard commercial invoices in Luxembourg. Invoices must be archived in a tamper-evident inventory system to satisfy AEDT audit requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: a 0% VAT rate applies where the goods are physically exported from the EU to a non-EU destination, evidenced by customs export declaration, transport documents, and proof of departure before or on the 90th day following supply. For services: fiduciary trust administration services rendered by a Luxembourg SARL to a non-EU business customer fall under the place-of-supply rule (Article 58 VAT Directive), placing supply outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT and resulting in an effective 0% charge without input VAT deduction. Where the customer is a private individual outside the EU, the services may still be zero-rated if they are ancillary to export/import of goods or if they fall under the B2C service list. In all cases, the exporter must hold contemporaneous commercial and accounting evidence demonstrating the non-EU status of the client and the actual cross-border performance, otherwise the standard 17% VAT will be assessed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Douane 2001) – required only for exports of physical goods; not applicable to pure service exports
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill – required only for goods exports as proof of exterior transit
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT confirmation) – required to evidence receipt of foreign proceeds and movement of funds from outside the EU
Service contract and detailed invoice showing the non-EU beneficially entitled entity and the place of effective use and enjoyment
Tax residence certificate or VAT identification number of the non-EU client, plus evidence of the client's business activity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg's ACD and AEDT scrutinise zero-rating claims through mandatory document reviews and post-clearance audits. If a zero-rated treatment is disallowed, the tax authority will issue an assessment for the unpaid VAT plus late-payment interest at 0.8% per month (or part thereof) and a penalty of up to 50% of the evaded tax in cases of wilful misstatement. Erroneous filings may attract a 10%–20% administrative surcharge. In cases of fraudulent export zero-rating – including false customs declarations, forged bills of lading, or simulated service contracts – the Luxembourg Criminal Code and Tax Fraud Act (Loi du 23 mars 2016) impose criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, together with a retrospective clawback of any refund with no limitation period for civil restitution where the underlying intent is fraudulent. The standard limitation for recovery of VAT is 10 years from the end of the year in which the tax became chargeable; this period is suspended upon the opening of a judicial audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) under the Eurosystem; CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) supervises all credit institutions and licensed professionals of the financial sector, including professional trustees.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full free movement of capital under Articles 63-66 TFEU; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions with EU/EEA counterparts. No exchange control authorization is required for inbound or outbound payments, but transactions between residents and non-residents exceeding €12,500 must be reported to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics. Profit remittances to non-EU shareholders may be subject to Luxembourg withholding tax (generally 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate holders, or 5% under certain DTTs); funds may be repatriated freely in EUR or any other currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion rules exist in Luxembourg. There is no obligation to repatriate receivables in EUR or to convert foreign currency balances; however, all cross-border receipts and payments relating to the SARL's fiduciary activity must be booked domestically in compliance with CSSF AML/CFT and accounting law, and must be declared to the BCL under the monthly/quarterly balance-of-payments reporting regime when the €12,500 threshold is exceeded.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for this high-risk special-license profile. Luxembourg-authorized EMIs (e.g., Mangopay S.A., PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. et Cie, S.C.A.) may provide payment initiation and e-money wallets, but most will reject a professional fiduciary trustee administering irrevocable offshore spendthrift trusts because such entities are classified as High_Risk_Special_License under CSSF Circular 20/744 and require a full FATF/AML framework, dedicated safeguarding accounts at a credit institution, and segregation of client funds. EMIs cannot substitute for the statutory segregated client-account structure and are not viable for escrow or settlement rails of the trust ledger.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical interview is effectively mandatory. Under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended), CSSF Circulars 18/698 and 20/744, and internal risk policies of Tier-1 banks, the authorised manager(s), beneficial owner(s), settlor (when the trust is being settled by the SARL), and protector/co-trustee must appear in person before the bank's compliance officer at onboarding. Remote or video-identification may be accepted only where a notarial or diplomatic certification (with apostille) has been produced after a physical meeting before a Luxembourg notary or a Luxembourg consular officer, and even then only at the bank's discretion. For discretionary asset-protection trusts, 100% of signatories and UBOs should expect a face-to-face opening interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unnamed discretionary beneficiaries; fallacy of 'beneficiary secrecy'
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust deed including all schedules and the discretionary beneficiary class definition, a signed protector consent, a side letter memorialising the settlor's wishes (non-binding), a written statutory statement of the trustee's fiduciary duties under Luxembourg Law of 27 July 2003, and a beneficiary class register (or, where beneficiaries are unascertained, a formal trustee attestation and independent legal opinion confirming enforceability and compliance with the Law of 27 July 2003 and the 1985 Hague Trusts Convention).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlor-retained powers creating sham or USA-risk exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Settlor power waiver/limitation deed, irrevocable and spendthrift clause extraction, independent trustee resolutions demonstrating the SARL's discretionary control, and a reputable U.S./international tax counsel opinion confirming non-sham status of the offshore irrevocable spendthrift trust; plus FATCA classification (W-8BEN-E / W-9 as applicable) and CRS registration certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth / source of funds opacity for trust corpus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited bank statements for the last 24 months from the funding account, sale and conveyance documents proving the origin of wealth, tax returns or stamp duty receipts, signed wealth-origin questionnaire, and independent accountants' confirmation of the trust settlement route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status of settlor, protector, or beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-certification forms for all relevant persons, mitigation justification from the bank's AML compliance, and source-of-funds evidence to the beyond-reasonable-doubt threshold; unacceptable if unexplained PEP-controlled political funds are the corpus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/Embargo exposure of the trust or its grantors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening certificate from a professional screening database (World-Check or equivalent) covering UBOs, beneficiaries, protector, and all counterparties; legal entity ownership cascade; and compliance manual comprising a sanctions policy, refusal-of-unregulated-funds policy, and training records aligned with EU Regulations 765/2006 and 269/2014 and OFAC screening.

CSSF licence or passporting documentation issued under Article 29-1 of the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, proof of professional indemnity insurance, audited financial statements, and the latest CSSF return confirming compliance with prudential solvency and AML conditions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for share capital and trust corpus settle via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank cover) in EUR using TARGET2/SEPA-instant clearing rails where possible. The routing protocol requires: (i) a dual-authority authenticated instruction from the SARL's manager and a co-signatory; (ii) a payment purpose code reflecting the settlement — 'CAPITAL INJECTION / SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARES' for the SARL's capital, and 'INITIAL TRUST SETTLEMENT / FIDUCIARY DEPOSIT' for the trust corpus; (iii) inclusion in Field 70 (Remittance Information) of the reference /BOP/ code and the CSSF transaction discrete-trust reference; and (iv) BCL cross-border balance-of-payments declaration within the statutory deadline for any inbound amount exceeding €12,500. Funds must be pre-cleared by the bank's sanctions engine; the bank may request a copy of the executed trust deed, the corporate authorisation, and the CSSF licence before credit is passed to the escrow ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements use the following clearing rails under the jurisdictional hierarchy: (1) SEPA EUR products (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD) for intra-EEA disbursements under €100,000; (2) SWIFT MT103 for global customer credit transfers, preferably with straight-through-processing and cover via MT202 for foreign-currency legs; (3) documentary trade finance rails — SWIFT MT700/MTA702 for standby/commercial letter of credit issuance against trustee disbursements, and collections via MT400/MT410; and (4) segregated high-value TARGET2 instructions for EUR payments above the RTGS threshold. Every outbound instruction must carry a specified disbursement purpose (e.g., 'BENEFICIARY DISTRIBUTION', 'INVESTMENT ASSET PURCHASE', 'ADMINISTRATION FEES'), the BCL balance-of-payments code, and an exact source-account designation referencing the segregated client money account rather than the firm's own house account, to preserve the trust's asset-partitioning under the Luxembourg Law of 27 July 2003 and CSSF Circular 20/744.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP forwards (vanilla forwards) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a bilaterally confirmed FX deal ticket with a Luxembourg-authorized credit institution

FX swaps (foreign-exchange swap / roll-over) for same-day liquidity management between EUR and USD, GBP, CHF, or HKD, permitted without mandatory clearing but subject to BCL EMIR reporting when outstanding notional exceeds BCL/ESMA thresholds

Cross-currency swaps (fixed-for-fixed or fixed-for-floating EUR/USD) for term-matched maturity of trust investment cash flows, cleared via LCH or CME where required under EMIR, or bilaterally with variation margin under the uncleared margin rules (BCBS-IOSCO/CSSF Circular)

EUR/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) and non-deliverable options (NDOs) are permissible only for converting emerging-market currency exposures where the underlying currency is non-convertible or restricted; must be cash-settled in EUR/USD, be executed with an EU-authorized credit institution, and be reported to the BCL with full underlying trade evidence

FX options and swaptions on EUR/USD and EUR/GBP for asymmetric hedging of trustee obligations, stated at-the-money, with premiums paid in EUR and no speculative open position beyond the trust's committed distribution schedule

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting minutes approving annual accounts, managers' discharge and allocation of results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the Luxembourg registered office; minutes are not separately filed with RCS unless publication is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year end; for an ordinary 31 December year-end, meeting must be held by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting does not create a direct government fine but prevents timely filing of annual accounts, exposes managers to civil liability and may lead to judicial enforcement upon shareholder application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filed (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes and management report when applicable) in the RCS e-filing format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the balance-sheet date; for an ordinary 31 December year-end, filing due by 31 July of the following year (or within one month of earlier approval by the shareholders' meeting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the entity to coercive fines, publication of non-compliance and potential administrative strike-off; managers may be held civilly liable for continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and annual net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year; the tax assessment notice may require a different filing date, and properly requested extensions are normally accommodated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest accrues at 0.5% per month on unpaid taxes; late-filing penalties apply in addition to default assessments; wilful non-filing may trigger criminal prosecution and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information in the RBE registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following the anniversary of the initial RBE declaration; in addition, any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for non-confirmation or inaccurate UBO data range up to EUR 25,000 for the legal entity and responsible managers; AML-supervisory enforcement may also apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT recapitulative statement for reportable cross-border intra-Community supplies and relevant cross-border services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing is permitted when the quarterly total of reportable supplies remains at or below the applicable threshold; otherwise the statement is filed quarterly, with each cover period following the prescribed calendar deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing assessments, interest on unpaid VAT and penalties apply; deliberate omissions are subject to criminal enforcement under Luxembourg VAT law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by an independent Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises is required when the undertaking exceeds at least two of the following three criteria over two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average number of employees 50. Certain regulated fiduciary activities may require audit irrespective of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as enacted under legislation transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for parent-company statutory accounts and generally required for consolidated financial statements of listed Luxembourg groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must initially file its beneficial owners with the RBE within 30 days of incorporation. Thereafter, an annual confirmation must be made within 30 days of the anniversary of the initial declaration. Any transfer of shares or change in control that affects UBO data requires an updated declaration within 30 days. The registered agent must verify supporting ownership documentation and update the AML/KYC file at each confirmation cycle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,000 per annum for Luxembourg registered office and corporate agent services, including registered-office address, domiciliation and filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,800 - USD 12,500 per year for a certified audit of a non-listed SARL; a restricted assurance or accountant confirmation service for an audit-exempt small SARL is typically USD 1,800 - USD 3,500 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for FY 2024/2025 in Luxembourg City, comprising 17.00% corporate income tax (CIT), 1.19% solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT), and 6.75% municipal business tax (ICC); a reduced CIT rate of 15% (16.05% with surcharge) applies to taxable income up to EUR 175,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Recurring structural reliefs: (i) 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (>=10% holding or >=EUR 6,000,000 acquisition cost for gains; >=10% or >=EUR 1,200,000 for dividends; 12-month holding period); (ii) IP box regime with 80% exemption of net IP income (grandfathered for assets acquired before 30 June 2021, sunset by 30 June 2024); (iii) R&D tax credit; (iv) rollover neutrality on qualifying reorganizations; (v) net wealth tax at 0.5% on net assets above EUR 500,000 with minimum tax of EUR 3,550 (financial assets >90% of balance sheet), EUR 1,605 (other standard cases), or EUR 535 (small entities).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward since FY 2017; no statutory cap; forfeited upon >50% change of control unless the same business activity is continued; minimum net wealth tax remains payable in loss years; no loss carryback)
